parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Define activity of a radioactive sample.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain why the variation with time of the activity of a radioactive sample is exponential in nature.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.lead:
A sample contains a single radioactive isotope that decays to form a stable isotope.

The sample has an activity of 180 Bq at time *t* = 0.
At a time 8.4 minutes later, the activity is 120 Bq.
parts.text: Determine the decay constant, in min⁻¹, of the radioactive isotope.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Use your answer in (c)(i) to determine the half-life, in min, of the radioactive isotope.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: On [[fig:f1]], sketch the variation of the activity *A* of the sample with *t* for values of *t* between *t* = 0 and *t* = 24 min.

figures.caption: Fig. 9.1
figures.alt: A blank graph grid with activity A / Bq on the vertical axis from 0 to 200 and time t / min on the horizontal axis from 0 to 24.
